name: aisc360-22
about: Rows of AISC 360-22 as two transcribers each wrote them (bench/formalizer), and the first types, grid and rules over them. The rules use LRFD. A grid line with no rule leaves its cell open.

gives.name: Rn
gives.what: nominal tensile or shear strength of one snug-tightened or pretensioned high-strength bolt or threaded part, for tension rupture or shear rupture

takes.name: Fn
takes.what: nominal stress of the fastener: the nominal tensile stress Fnt or the nominal shear stress Fnv of Table J3.2

takes.name: Ab
takes.what: nominal area of the unthreaded body of the bolt or threaded part

gives.name: Fnt_prime
gives.what: nominal tensile stress of a bolt in a bearing-type connection, reduced for the shear stress that acts with the tension, LRFD; the standard writes it as Fnt with a prime on the F

takes.name: Fnt
takes.what: nominal tensile stress of the fastener from Table J3.2

takes.name: Fnv
takes.what: nominal shear stress of the fastener from Table J3.2

takes.name: frv
takes.what: required shear stress in the bolt under LRFD load combinations; the clause requires it to be no more than the available shear stress, 0.75 Fnv

gives.name: Rn

takes.name: d

takes.name: t
takes.what: thickness of the connected material

takes.name: Fu

gives.name: Rn

takes.name: lc
takes.what: clear distance, in the direction of the force, from the edge of the hole to the edge of the next hole or to the edge of the material

takes.name: t
takes.what: thickness of the connected material

takes.name: Fu
takes.what: specified minimum tensile strength of the connected material

takes.name: Anv

takes.name: h
takes.what: clear depth of the web: between flanges less the fillets for a rolled shape, between flanges for a welded built-up section, between fastener lines for a bolted built-up section

takes.name: tw

takes.name: kv

takes.name: tw
takes.what: thickness of the web

takes.name: k
takes.what: distance from the outer face of the flange to the web toe of the fillet

takes.name: lb

takes.name: d
takes.what: full nominal depth of the member

jumps.why: The standard gives one formula for a force farther than d from the member end and another for a force within d of it, and switches between them at x = d by a step. Away from the end the yielding spreads along the web to both sides of the force and the length counted through k is 5k; near the end it can spread to one side only and the standard counts 2.5k.

gives.name: Rn
gives.what: nominal strength of the web for the limit state of web local crippling under a concentrated compressive force applied normal to the flange

takes.what: length of bearing

takes.name: x
takes.what: distance from the member end to the point where the concentrated compressive force is applied

takes.name: Qf
takes.what: chord-stress interaction parameter: 1.0 for wide-flange sections, channels, box sections and HSS with the connecting surface in tension, otherwise from Section K1.3

jumps.why: The standard gives one formula for a force at least d/2 from the member end, with the coefficient 0.80, and two for a force nearer the end, with the coefficient 0.40, and switches between them at x = d/2 by a step: a force near the end has web on one side only to resist crippling. The two end formulas meet at lb/d = 0.2.

The standard gives one formula for a force at least d/2 from the member end, with the coefficient 0.80, and two for a force nearer the end, with the coefficient 0.40, and switches between them at x = d/2 by a step: a force near the end has web on one side only to resist crippling. The two end formulas meet at lb/d = 0.2.

fields.name: Fu

types.what: one line of two or more bolts in single shear through two plates, in a bearing-type joint that is pulled along the line

fields.name: fastener
fields.what: the strength group of the bolts, as Section J3.2 names it

fields.name: threads

grid.what: whether the bolts must be pretensioned or the joint slip-critical
whether this type of hole may be used in this joint
minimum distance from an end hole to the end of a plate
minimum distance from a hole to the side edge of a plate
shear of the bolts with bearing and tearout at their holes
tension on the bolts together with shear

unless.why: a lap carries a pull along its line, which shears its bolts and puts no tension on them
a lap is a bearing-type joint, which claims no slip resistance

grid.what: tensile rupture of each plate through its holes
shear of a plate as an element loaded in shear

unless.why: the plates of a lap are pulled along its line; shear on their planes beside the bolts is tearout and block shear

grid.what: block shear rupture of each plate
yielding and buckling of a plate in compression

unless.why: the load on a lap is a pull, which the card signs as at least zero

grid.what: bending of the plates, which a lap in single shear sets apart

rules.says: the pull is at most 0.75 of the sum over the bolts of the least of a bolt's shear strength and the bearing and tearout strengths at its two holes

where.why: the line of bolts is at most 38 inch long (note c of Table J3.2 lowers the shear stress of a longer one, and this rule does not)

rules.says: the distance from the centre of an end hole to the end of a plate is at least the table's value for the bolt diameter
the pull is at most 0.90 of the yield strength of the gross section of the first plate
the pull is at most 0.90 of the yield strength of the gross section of the second plate
